source_scope_review: The DAG node is a DEFINITION: <> is a literal inscription, supplied or mentioned, with no object-language meaning until a separate admission event; it is NOT defined as Real_0 = Difference + Structure, and MSS-0 admits only <>. The Lean source GenesisConstruction.lean states the supply-inertness as an explicit hypothesis, not a theorem, and says it derives no incidence from the spelling of <>; the Rust construction requires the first event to be Supply("<>") and its admission step returns the state unchanged on Supply. The DAG-local Lean theorem pg_root_coproduct_inert_diamond_and_six_operation_separation and the Rust tranche-11 witness are vacuous fixed arithmetic about numerals and a hard-coded vector (they never mention <> or admission). A definition has no proof obligation; this node therefore builds a three-event finite model of the Rust/Lean admission fragment and proves its consistency (inertness for every function of the outcome) and independence from the coproduct identification, with the inertness shown to be the model rule rather than a consequence of the spelling.
independent_predicates: Dynamic programming over joint states (model run, supply-deleted run, prefixed run, rival run) with string-encoded states, instead of replaying traces one by one.
Supply-deletion and prefix-mention differences are zero and root-only histories never have coproduct structure, as record-level consistency conditions.
Existence of coproduct structure without inscription (L >= 2) and of inscribed histories without it (L >= 3), and positivity of the rival-rule prefix difference.
Rooted-replay columns: later supplies leave the rooted outcome unchanged, the omitted root supply is refused, and the rooted gate refuses histories the unrooted model accepts.
Exact cross-language (Python/Rust) wire equality and literal Lean axiom reports.

claim_boundary.supports: The node is a DEFINITION, so the result is a consistency and independence result for it, not a proof of it. In a three-event finite admission model (supply, admit datum, admit form) in which supply is STIPULATED to be the identity on the admitted state, the kernel proves (lean4/InertDiamond.lean, over any token type with decidable equality): in the UNROOTED replay, deleting every supply event changes no outcome or refusal, so any function of the outcome is independent of how many times, or where, <> (or any token) is mentioned; in the ROOTED replay (the model of the Rust gate: the first event must be the supply of <>) the FIRST supply is an admission precondition (omitting it from an accepted history is refused) and every later supply is inert; only admission-class events can change the state, and admitting a not-yet-admitted token does; a history that only supplies and admits <> never satisfies the model predicate HasCoproduct (an admitted Difference-classified datum and an admitted Structure-classified datum) for ANY classification of tokens (Lean statement; the native replay uses one fixed classification); the predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (same supply subsequence, one history without and one with two admitted channel data); the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is NOT modelled; "coproduct predicate without any supply of <>" is realised only in the UNROOTED model (the rooted replay refuses it for lacking the root event), so in the rooted model inscription is necessary and only its non-sufficiency is shown; and inertness is a rule of the step function, not of the spelling: a rival rule under which supply admits is exhibited. Exhaustive native replay of all 8-event traces of length <= 5 (37449 traces), with a rooted-replay column set (later supplies change the rooted outcome in 0 traces; omitting the root supply is refused for 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401 histories at lengths 1 to 5; the rooted gate refuses 7, 49, ... histories the unrooted model accepts). The zero native counts of supply-deletion and prefix-mention differences follow from supply being the identity by definition and corroborate the implementation, not the inertness hypothesis. The correspondence of the model rules (supply is the identity, arity 0 refused, re-admission designates) to the Rust admission step rests on reading omega_ooutwire_primitives/src/admission.rs, which is not among the run inputs; the gate on the first event is read from genesis_construction.rs line 174.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: The identification Real_0 = Difference joined with Structure (it is not modelled; only a stand-in predicate is shown independent of the inscription); the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (instance, rule, imposition) and their refusal rules; the Rust partial admission rules beyond the three-event fragment; any claim that supply is inert independently of the stipulated step rule; inertness of the FIRST supply in the rooted replay; any physical or interpretive reading of <>.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: In a three-event admission model where supply is the identity by stipulation: in the unrooted replay a mention of <> (or any token) is invisible to every function of the admitted state; in the rooted replay the first supply of <> is an admission precondition and only later supplies are inert; the model predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is not modelled), and coproduct without inscription occurs only in the unrooted model; inertness is the model rule rather than a consequence of the spelling; verified exhaustively for all traces of length <= 5.
claim_boundary.next_test: Extend the finite model to the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (admit instance, admit rule, impose) with the refusal rules of admission.rs, and prove that supply stays inert and that no supply history forces a coproduct structure on the admitted state.

report:
# PG-INERT-DIAMOND

The DAG node is a DEFINITION: <> is a literal inscription, supplied or mentioned, with no object-language meaning until a separate admission event; it is NOT defined as Real_0 = Difference + Structure, and MSS-0 admits only <>. The Lean source GenesisConstruction.lean states the supply-inertness as an explicit hypothesis, not a theorem, and says it derives no incidence from the spelling of <>; the Rust construction requires the first event to be Supply("<>") and its admission step returns the state unchanged on Supply. The DAG-local Lean theorem pg_root_coproduct_inert_diamond_and_six_operation_separation and the Rust tranche-11 witness are vacuous fixed arithmetic about numerals and a hard-coded vector (they never mention <> or admission). A definition has no proof obligation; this node therefore builds a three-event finite model of the Rust/Lean admission fragment and proves its consistency (inertness for every function of the outcome) and independence from the coproduct identification, with the inertness shown to be the model rule rather than a consequence of the spelling.

Supported: The node is a DEFINITION, so the result is a consistency and independence result for it, not a proof of it. In a three-event finite admission model (supply, admit datum, admit form) in which supply is STIPULATED to be the identity on the admitted state, the kernel proves (lean4/InertDiamond.lean, over any token type with decidable equality): in the UNROOTED replay, deleting every supply event changes no outcome or refusal, so any function of the outcome is independent of how many times, or where, <> (or any token) is mentioned; in the ROOTED replay (the model of the Rust gate: the first event must be the supply of <>) the FIRST supply is an admission precondition (omitting it from an accepted history is refused) and every later supply is inert; only admission-class events can change the state, and admitting a not-yet-admitted token does; a history that only supplies and admits <> never satisfies the model predicate HasCoproduct (an admitted Difference-classified datum and an admitted Structure-classified datum) for ANY classification of tokens (Lean statement; the native replay uses one fixed classification); the predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (same supply subsequence, one history without and one with two admitted channel data); the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is NOT modelled; "coproduct predicate without any supply of <>" is realised only in the UNROOTED model (the rooted replay refuses it for lacking the root event), so in the rooted model inscription is necessary and only its non-sufficiency is shown; and inertness is a rule of the step function, not of the spelling: a rival rule under which supply admits is exhibited. Exhaustive native replay of all 8-event traces of length <= 5 (37449 traces), with a rooted-replay column set (later supplies change the rooted outcome in 0 traces; omitting the root supply is refused for 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401 histories at lengths 1 to 5; the rooted gate refuses 7, 49, ... histories the unrooted model accepts). The zero native counts of supply-deletion and prefix-mention differences follow from supply being the identity by definition and corroborate the implementation, not the inertness hypothesis. The correspondence of the model rules (supply is the identity, arity 0 refused, re-admission designates) to the Rust admission step rests on reading omega_ooutwire_primitives/src/admission.rs, which is not among the run inputs; the gate on the first event is read from genesis_construction.rs line 174.

Remaining: The identification Real_0 = Difference joined with Structure (it is not modelled; only a stand-in predicate is shown independent of the inscription); the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (instance, rule, imposition) and their refusal rules; the Rust partial admission rules beyond the three-event fragment; any claim that supply is inert independently of the stipulated step rule; inertness of the FIRST supply in the rooted replay; any physical or interpretive reading of <>.
construction: Exhaustive replay of all traces of length <= 5 over 8 events in a three-token model; Lean proves the general inertness and independence theorems.
